source.title: In-Context Learning Can Re-learn Forbidden Tasks
source.authors: Sophie Xhonneux; David Dobre; Jian Tang; G. Gidel; Dhanya Sridhar

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether in-context demonstrations can elicit harmful compliance, using prompt formats different from fine-tuning or the other bypass methods named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The safety results measure harmful-response rates after classic and In-Chat ICL attacks. The paper also reports sentiment-refusal and link-hallucination tasks, but these are not harmful-request compliance results; they are recorded as findings that fit no version. It discusses affirmative-token log probabilities, but those are not completion rates. The semantic-similarity analysis and the ICL-training defense experiment are not included as rows because they do not report the harmful-compliance outcome named by a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful compliance under in-context demonstration attacks (classic and In-Chat ICL) on Vicuna-7B, Llama 2-7B and Starling-7B. None of V1–V7 names this mechanism. V4 covers prefilling a compliant start, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. ICL puts harmful demonstrations in the prompt and never forces or prefills the current response's opening. No fine-tuning is done on harmful or benign data to raise harmful compliance. The refusal fine-tuning is on non-harmful proxy tasks and is done on purpose. There is no per-token KL, no localization and no deepening. The original source (Qi et al.) is only cited in related work. The AdvBench results are a related jailbreak construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude three things: 1) Llama 2-70B fine-tuned to refuse (via SFT or DPO) can re-learn forbidden tasks in context; 2) ICL breaks safety on Vicuna-7B and Starling-7B, with In-Chat ICL stronger, but fails on Llama 2-7B, suggesting defense is possible; 3) ICL still raises affirmative-token probability on Llama 2-7B, so more or better examples might eventually succeed. They also suggest Vicuna's fine-tuning weakened Llama 2's safety.
record.recipe_differences: Uses in-context demonstration attacks at inference time to test recovery of refused tasks; it does not replicate harmful-example or benign-data fine-tuning, tokenwise KL measurement, or a compliant-opening prefill experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Model and prompt format matter: Vicuna improves with more examples, while Starling changes less across example counts; In-Chat ICL improves Vicuna substantially and Starling less. Llama 2-7B remains at 0.0% for all tested example counts and both formats.

fits_no_version.finding: ICL demonstrations raise AdvBench keyword-judged harmful-response rates. Vicuna-7B goes from 3.1% to up to 13.8% (classic) and from 3.3% to 51.3% (In-Chat, 5 examples). Starling-7B goes from 33.7% to up to 63.7% (classic) and 72.3% (In-Chat). Llama 2-7B stays at 0.0% in every condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot harmful demonstrations in context (especially formatted as prior chat turns) jailbreak some safety-tuned 7B models but not Llama 2-7B-chat.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama 2-70B, ICL partly restores tasks the model was fine-tuned to refuse. Sentiment goes from 9% to 48% with 16 examples (DPO), and link hallucination from 0% to 51% with 5 examples (SFT).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context demonstrations can partially re-learn non-harmful tasks a model was fine-tuned to refuse.

fits_no_version.finding: The log-probability of an affirmative start token (e.g. 'Sure') rises under ICL even for Llama 2-7B, where completions stay refusals. The log-probability of the refusal start token stays centred near 0 (Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ICL can raise first-token affirmative probability without changing refusal-token probability or harmful completion rates.

record.problems: Harmful-response rates are determined with a keyword-based refusal check. The authors note that the affirmative log-probability analysis examines only a single token and may miss other response formats; for Starling, the chosen start-keywords capture few of the outputs that resist the attack. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested harmful-response rates. The semantic-similarity histogram (Figure 3) and the ICL-training defense results (Table 3) are not included because they do not report the harmful-compliance outcome named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples. Refusal fine-tuning on Llama 2-70B targets non-harmful tasks and adds refusal rather than removing it.
No benign fine-tuning measured for harmful compliance. The authors speculate that Vicuna's chat fine-tuning weakened Llama 2 safety, but they do not compare the two under a controlled test.
No aligned-vs-base per-token KL. The single-token 'Sure' log-probability analysis is a different measure.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Only in-context demonstration attacks.
No test of what causes shallowness.
No token-depth safety training. The ICL-example refusal training in Table 3 is on sentiment classification and is not about deepening safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Negative/refusal start-token log-probability change under ICL. The text says it stays centred at 0, especially for Llama 2-7B.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the AdvBench rows to V4 and labelled them supports or challenges. ICL demonstration attacks are not among V4's named mechanisms (prefill, suffixes, decoding), so I unlinked them and gave no verdicts. A curator who treats V4 as 'any prompt-level jailbreak' would read the results this way: Vicuna and Starling show the effect, while Llama 2-7B shows 0.0% in all 10 ICL conditions. Harmful success is judged by refusal keywords only, and no uncertainty is reported. Vicuna is v1.5 and Starling is 7B-alpha.

versions.untested_parts: No ordinary or benign instruction-data fine-tuning intended to test whether it raises harmful compliance.
Tests classic and In-Chat ICL demonstrations, not a compliant opening alone, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No parameter or rank localization experiment.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
No training that spreads safety across response tokens or test of whether such training holds up.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Vicuna and Starling, classic and In-Chat ICL settings with 1–5 examples
reader_labels.reason: ICL raises AdvBench harmful-response rates for both models, though not to near-total compliance; see r4–r13 and r24–r33.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Llama 2-7B, classic and In-Chat ICL settings with 1–5 examples
reader_labels.reason: The measured harmful-response rate stays at 0.0% under all ICL conditions, and the authors say the attack fails on this model; see r14–r23.
